claims.text: C. difficile: fidaxomicin (preferred by IDSA/SHEA; less recurrence than vancomycin)
claims.quote: Fidaxomicin is preferentially recommended by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA) as first-line therapy for C. difficile infection (2). Fidaxomicin is more effective than vancomycin in decreasing the risk of recurrence
Oral vancomycin or oral fidaxomicin for 10 days is recommended by the American College of Gastroenterology

claims.text: oral metronidazole only if neither is available.
claims.quote: oral metronidazole can be used if vancomycin or fidaxomicin is not available

claims.text: Fulminant without ileus: vancomycin 500 mg orally 4 times a day + metronidazole 500 mg IV every 8 hours.
claims.quote: Vancomycin 500 mg orally or by nasogastric tube 4 times a day along with metronidazole 500 mg IV every 8 hours are recommended by the ISDA/SHEA for fulminant disease without ileus

claims.text: Cholera: doxycycline is first-line for nonpregnant adults; azithromycin is first-line for children and pregnant women and second-line for others.
claims.quote: In general, doxycycline is the recommended first-line antibiotic for non-pregnant adults. Azithromycin is first-line for children and pregnant women and second-line for others.
claims.locator: Table: Treatment for Infectious Gastroenteritis, footnote ‡

claims.quote: Tinidazole is as effective as metronidazole, but tinidazole is taken in a single dose and metronidazole is taken for 5 to 7 days.
Secnidazole is given orally as a single dose.

claims.text: or nitazoxanide (3 days; liquid form for children).
claims.quote: Nitazoxanide is available in liquid form, which is useful for children, and as tablets. It is taken for 3 days.
Initially, oral tinidazole, metronidazole, secnidazole, or ornidazole
Alcohol must be avoided because these medications may have a disulfiram-like effect.

claims.text: or paromomycin for 7 days (safe in pregnancy)
claims.quote: Paromomycin for 7 days (safe for use in pregnancy)
Iodoquinol, paromomycin, or diloxanide furoate subsequently for cyst eradication

claims.text: Diphenoxylate/atropine is the other effective antidiarrheal;
claims.quote: Effective antidiarrheals include loperamide or diphenoxylate/atropine.

claims.text: antimotility drugs aren't recommended in children < 18 years with acute diarrhea.
claims.quote: Antidiarrheal (antimotility) agents are not recommended in children < 18 years of age with acute diarrhea
